title: TCP: Regression fix MSP with out-of-order preference
description: When running with tcp.reassemble_out_of_order:true, a retransmitted packet might cause the value of tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq to decrease.

requested review from @eugene.adell

I haven't found anything wrong with my set of PCAPs, then may I ask a PCAP showing this behavior _wireshark to no longer be able to properly reorder packets afterwards_ ? Maybe something is wrong when 2 packets are retransmitted but arrive in the wrong order ?

This test you want to add was there in earlier versions, but was removed when the reassembly was heavily reworked.

Yeah sure! I have a pcap here that I have anonymized.

[broken_example.pcap](/uploads/121ba56507324bb6d7ddfcef2d80d980/broken_example.pcap)

If I enable tcp.reassemble_out_of_order and look at packet number 12, it can extract one TLS PDU from the tcp segment, but it doesnt recognize the last 48 bytes as TLS and classifies them as "TCP Segment data". After this point, wireshark doesn't seem to be able to interpret any data at all as TLS. For example, packet 37 contains the start of a TLS PDU, but it is not parsed as such.

When I look at the value of tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq while parsing these packetets, I get the following values:

packet 6: 5553

packet 8: 6941

packet 9: 2777

The value of tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq seems to have decreased, and it seems to me as if that might not be desirable. If I apply the patch and prevent tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq from decreasing, the packets are parsed as is expected.

This behaviour doesn't show up if I disable tcp.reassemble_out_of_order. 

Also, if I run an older version of wireshark (3.6.1), the packets are parsed correctly even with tcp.reassemble_out_of_order enabled.

With your MR we now see p29 being part of two MSPs, the second one being reassembled in p32, which is the desired behavior.

However the issue happens when we explicitly ask for OOO reassembly, while your PCAP doesn't show any OOO (we can see Dup ACKs and Retransmissions only).
Because of this, the fix is good but not at the right place. You are rewriting some code which was there, but removed when the reassembly was re-worked heavily some time ago.

May I also suggest to _amend_ then the title mentions it's a regression fix on MSP with out-of-order preference , and the message then its width is similar to other commit messages (the comments when commiting should help you) ?

Thanks for the feedback!

Ive changed the commit to have a better title and a matching message.

The PCAP I provided was an excerpt from a much larger PCAP, which does have actual OOO packets that require me to use the tcp.reassemble_out_of_order preference. The same tcp session as the one in the provided PCAP also has out-of-order packets earlier in the session. If it helps, I could try to provide this part of the PCAP as well?

I'm afraid I don't really catch your meaning about the fix not being in the right place. Do you think I should look for another place to perform the check on tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq?

Yes, this works as well! I do have to remove this line then as well, but it seems redundant after your suggestion:

```
5026            /* Update the maximum expected seqno if no SYN packet was seen
5027            * before, or if the new segment succeeds previous segments. */
5028            tcpd->fwd->maxnextseq = nxtseq;
```

One thing I am not sure about though, is that the function `msp_add_out_of_order`  also seems to do things with tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq, and then the updated value will not yet be available when it is called. I'm not sure whether or not that will be an issue.

Do you think I should update the commit to your suggestion?

it's redundant but I'm very conservative.. so keep it please (you still can comment _XXX - looks redundant with later code_). The only issue we've seen so far is that specific case of OOO preference having a side effect when there's no OOO :| Share your new updated code and I'll test it with a bunch of PCAPs.

Ah, sadly if I leave the line, the error is still present, probably because the value of tcpd-\>fwd-\>maxnextseq is still being decreased in that line.

Btw, thanks for all the help so far!
please push and update your branch so I can see
Yes, I've, updated the branch

Yes, that fixes it as well, thank you!

Ive updated the branch, and updated the comments regarding the modified statements as well.
Hm, it seems that it is now failing the pipeline, and that it doesn't parse all the tests correctly?

that's an artifact upload, probably a timeout with no consequence.
Meanwhile I'm testing the MR, it seems the very first one you wrote was better. I'll answer later, still testing on different PCAPs as this part may have many side effects.

I finished testing the different possibilities with some captures. The very first version you sent (test on LT_SEQ and 0 value) is the one which improves things and has no side-effect, and the suggestions I made aren't necessary. You can resubmit this one and I'll resolve threads/merge. Sorry for the delay but this part requires things to be clean.

Ive just resubmitted the first commit. Thanks for all your effort into this issue!

No worries about the delay, I'd much rather do this properly and securely than rushing it!
OK that's good.
